blocks.text:
Beyond the salt flat, the road follows a chain of snow-capped volcanoes into the Lípez region. Ollagüe Volcano is visible in the distance.

The route then crosses the Eduardo Avaroa National Reserve. Along the way, you stop at four high-altitude lagoons known collectively as the Joyas Altoandinas: Cañapa, Hedionda, Chiarkota and Honda. Look out for local birds and see how water, salt and volcanic mountains shape the colours of the landscape.

By evening you reach the Siloli Desert. There are stops for photographs, and you spend the night at a hotel in the high desert.

Included: one night at Hotel Tayka del Desierto, private 4×4 transport, a bilingual English- and Spanish-speaking guide, and admission fees. Meals: breakfast, lunch and dinner.
Flamingos in the shallows of Laguna Cañapa, surrounded by salt-lined shores and volcanic mountains in Bolivia
Cañapa, a high-altitude lagoon with flamingos in Bolivia
Siloli Desert, Laguna Verde and Uyuni

We set off at around 05:30. First you see the Stone Tree, then continue through the Eduardo Avaroa National Reserve to the Sol de Mañana Geysers. Steam and gases rise from the ground, and nearby mud pools bubble in shades of red and grey.

After visiting the geysers, you can bathe in the hot springs. The road then crosses the Dalí Desert, with its wind-sculpted stone columns, to reach Laguna Verde at the foot of Licancabur Volcano.

On the way back, you visit Laguna Colorada, where algae and plankton turn the water shades of brown and deep red. Three species of flamingo nest here: James’s, Andean and Chilean flamingos.

In the afternoon, the road passes through the Valley of the Rocks, with volcanic formations around 8–15 m tall. The final stop is the village of San Cristóbal. You arrive in Uyuni at approximately 18:00.

Included: one night at Jardines de Uyuni Hotel or a hotel of the same category, private 4×4 transport, a bilingual guide and admission fees. Meals: breakfast and lunch.
